Subject: Controlled-access addendum / audit requests

Hi David —

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal and procurement reviewed the MSA + Order Form and have a few follow-ups specific to our Private VPC delivery: scope of license for operator activities, audit access windows, and what you can commit to for evidence retention.

Attached is a draft matrix of artifacts we think we'll need for a quarterly audit (audit-evidence-matrix.xlsx). Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood will include an addendum granting a limited "operator" license for on-prem agents vs. a tenant-only license?
- Proposed timeline for an audit window (we prefer a 30-day window, with a 3-business-day notice for remote review and a 10-business-day window for onsite witness)
- Whether you offer a sealed-snapshot escrow or a witness model for snapshot validation (we can accept a witnessed snapshot if you provide logroot/hash and a witness runbook)

Can you loop in legal? Procurement would like a calendar proposal by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Lane
Senior Program Manager — Lumen Health

Attachment: audit-evidence-matrix.xlsx

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-09T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Controlled-access addendum / audit requests

Hi Emma —

Appreciate the clear matrix. Quick answers up front:
- We can provide an MSA addendum that carves an "Operator" role limited to running the runtime and performing maintenance; no access to tenant plaintext data unless explicitly surfaced via customer-approved support sessions. That language will be captured as a license boundary (we'll propose explicit operator APIs and cryptographic seal points).
- We can support both remote review and an onsite witness. Our standard offering is: 3-business-day remote notice for read-only artifact access, a 30-day remote review window, and a 7-business-day window for onsite witness scheduling. We can extend onsite windows to 10 business days on a per-deal basis as a concession.
- For snapshot verification, we offer a witnessed-snapshot model (operator creates snapshots, hashes are shared, witness verifies with our steward) and a sealed-escrow variant with a third-party custodian for highly regulated customers.

I attached a first-pass addendum (LF-Addendum_v2.docx) with the license boundary language and an appendix describing evidence we can provide (runbooks, KV-access logs, operator session artifacts, and signed hash manifests). Please note the addendum still contains placeholders for a few SLAs.

Proposed schedule:
- Thu 2028-11-16: Redwood to send redline (we'll target clean PDF + tracked .docx)
- Tue 2028-11-21: Joint legal sync call (30m)
- Week of 2028-12-04: Preliminary remote artifact handoff (as per matrix)

If that works, I'll ask Marissa to prepare the evidence matrix from our side and Naomi to confirm runbook artifact availability.

Best,
David
David Kim
Head of Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachment: LF-Addendum_v2.docx

Thanks David and Naomi — this is helpful. I'm copying Gina from Lumen Legal to coordinate redlines.

Gina: our ask is a narrow addendum that:
- Limits operator rights to maintenance and run-only duties, with explicit prohibition on data exfiltration
- Defines the audit windows and notice periods (we'd prefer the 30-day remote window + 10-business-day onsite option you proposed, but procurement will confirm)
- Specifies retention periods for signed hashes and manifests (180 days is acceptable if you can commit in-contract)
- For escrow/witness: we are open to witnessed snapshots if you provide the witness runbook and a hash manifest; otherwise we'd like a third-party escrow option described as a fallback.

Can Redwood send a clean PDF of the addendum and a side-by-side redline by EOD Wednesday 2028-11-15? Also confirm whether the addendum needs a separate exhibit on the Order Form or whether we should reference it from the MSA (Lumen prefers a referenced exhibit to the MSA).

Regards,
Emma
